title: Hidden Conformal Boundary Data in Finite-Temperature Stabilizer Entropy
abstract: The finite-temperature stabilizer Renyi entropy (index 1/2) of the open critical transverse-field Ising chain is expressed as a sum over absolute square-minors of a finite-T correlation matrix and reduced exactly to a single Pfaffian with block Toeplitz-Hankel structure. In the crossover regime beta proportional to L the stabilizer entropy factorizes into an extensive piece plus a universal finite-size scaling function that is a level-8 eta quotient (not the ordinary free-boundary Majorana thermal factor), yielding a Cardy-like asymptotic and revealing defect-like conformal data invisible to ordinary thermodynamic probes.
key_claims: Finite-T stabilizer Renyi entropy of the critical TFIM reduces exactly to a Pfaffian (block Toeplitz-Hankel), same free-fermion correlation-matrix formalism as exact-diagonalization force measurements.
Universal finite-size scaling function in the beta~L regime is a level-8 eta quotient with a Cardy-like asymptotic.
Reveals defect-like / boundary conformal data invisible to thermodynamic probes -- a finite-T-only sensitivity.
